name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's roughly 22-point Republican partisan lean anchors the fundamentals
Griffith's dominant fundraising: $2.2M raised and $879K on hand versus $257K for Powers
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 97% to win
No polls, expert ratings, or outside spending signal a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's twenty-two-point Republican lean, Griffith's overwhelming financial advantage as the incumbent, and markets pricing his reelection near certain leave no evidence of a competitive contest, so the forecast rests on fundamentals with no basis to move.
model.watch: Any late infusion of Democratic outside spending or a poll showing Griffith below 60% would be the first sign the race is moving.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Virginia's ninth district is deeply Republican territory, and incumbent Morgan Griffith is seeking another term with the structural advantages that come with it. The district's partisan lean of roughly twenty-two points Republican forms the backbone of the race's fundamentals, and no general-election polling has emerged to suggest the contest is competitive. Prediction markets give Democratic nominee Joy Powers only a few percent chance of an upset.

Powers has raised about $257,000 with almost no outside help, while Griffith has brought in more than $2.1 million and holds a large cash-on-hand advantage. No outside groups have spent against the incumbent, and no major rating organizations have flagged the seat as in play. The forecast therefore rests on district fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Republican win, with uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling rather than any sign of a genuine race.
